export function relativeTime(value: Date | string | null | undefined): string {
  if (!value) return "—";
  const date = typeof value === "string" ? new Date(value) : value;
  const seconds = Math.round((date.getTime() - Date.now()) / 1000);
  const formatter = new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat("en-US", { numeric: "auto" });
  const units: [Intl.RelativeTimeFormatUnit, number][] = [
    ["year", 31536000],
    ["month", 2592000],
    ["week", 604800],
    ["day", 86400],
    ["hour", 3600],
    ["minute", 60],
    ["second", 1],
  ];
  for (const [unit, size] of units) {
    if (Math.abs(seconds) >= size || unit === "second") {
      return formatter.format(Math.round(seconds / size), unit);
    }
  }
  return "now";
}

export type RuleSource = "CUSTOM" | "SECRET" | "SCA" | "LICENSE";

export interface FileContext {
  /** Repository-relative path, always POSIX separators. */
  path: string;
  content: string;
  lines: string[];
  ext: string;
}

export interface RuleMatch {
  lineStart: number;
  lineEnd?: number;
  /** Stable evidence used to build a re-scan fingerprint. Never contains raw secrets. */
  evidence: string;
  /** Optional pre-rendered, redacted snippet. */
  snippet?: string;
  title?: string;
  severity?: Severity;
  confidence?: number;
  description?: string;
  remediation?: string;
  owasp?: string;
  category?: string;
}

export interface Rule {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  severity: Severity;
  confidence: number;
  source: RuleSource;
  owasp: string;
  category: string;
  description: string;
  remediation: string;
  appliesTo?: (ctx: FileContext) => boolean;
  find: (ctx: FileContext) => RuleMatch[];
}

export interface RawFinding {
  ruleId: string;
  source: RuleSource;
  title: string;
  severity: Severity;
  owasp: string;
  category: string;
  filePath: string;
  lineStart: number;
  lineEnd: number;
  snippet: string;
  description: string;
  remediation: string;
  confidence: number;
  fingerprint: string;
}

export type SeverityCounts = Record<Severity, number>;

export interface ScanResult {
  findings: RawFinding[];
  filesScanned: number;
  bytesScanned: number;
  skippedFiles: number;
  truncated: boolean;
  durationMs: number;
  engineVersion: string;
  score: number;
  grade: string;
  counts: SeverityCounts;
}

export interface ScanLimits {
  maxFiles: number;
  maxTotalBytes: number;
  maxFileBytes: number;
  maxFindings: number;
}

export const DEFAULT_SCAN_LIMITS: ScanLimits = {
  maxFiles: 2500,
  maxTotalBytes: 30 * 1024 * 1024,
  maxFileBytes: 1024 * 1024,
  maxFindings: 500,
};

export const ENGINE_VERSION = "vibecheck-engine/0.1.0";

export function lineAt(content: string, index: number): number {
  let line = 1;
  for (let i = 0; i < index && i < content.length; i += 1) {
    if (content.charCodeAt(i) === 10) line += 1;
  }
  return line;
}

export function lineTextAt(lines: string[], line: number): string {
  return (lines[line - 1] ?? "").trim();
}

export function snippetAround(
  lines: string[],
  start: number,
  end: number,
  padding = 1,
): string {
  const from = Math.max(0, start - 1 - padding);
  const to = Math.min(lines.length, end + padding);
  return lines.slice(from, to).join("\n").slice(0, 1600);
}

export function restrictiveLicense(
  license: string,
): { restricted: boolean; severity: Severity; label: string } | null {
  const normalized = license.trim();
  if (!normalized) return null;
  if (/^AGPL/i.test(normalized)) {
    return { restricted: true, severity: "CRITICAL", label: normalized };
  }
  if (/^(?:SSPL|BUSL|BSL)/i.test(normalized)) {
    return { restricted: true, severity: "HIGH", label: normalized };
  }
  if (/^GPL/i.test(normalized)) {
    return { restricted: true, severity: "HIGH", label: normalized };
  }
  if (/Elastic-2\.0|Commons Clause|CC-BY-NC/i.test(normalized)) {
    return { restricted: true, severity: "HIGH", label: normalized };
  }
  if (/^LGPL/i.test(normalized)) {
    return { restricted: true, severity: "MEDIUM", label: normalized };
  }
  return null;
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"csVEM_2wNtk","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"scripts/purge-sources.ts","instructions":"Implement the age-based source retention purge job.","content":"import { promises as fs } from "node:fs";
import { and, eq, isNotNull } from "drizzle-orm";
import { db } from "../src/db";
import {
  auditLogs,
  engagements,
  organizations,
  scanRuns,
} from "../src/db/schema";
import { purgeSource } from "../src/lib/ingest";

const DEFAULT_DAYS = 30;

async function main() {
  const days = Number.parseInt(
    process.env.SOURCE_RETENTION_DAYS ?? String(DEFAULT_DAYS),
    10,
  );
  if (!Number.isFinite(days) || days < 0) {
    throw new Error("SOURCE_RETENTION_DAYS must be a non-negative number");
  }
  const forceAll = process.argv.includes("--all");
  const cutoff = Date.now() - days * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

  const rows = await db
    .select({
      scan: scanRuns,
      engagement: engagements,
      org: organizations,
    })
    .from(scanRuns)
    .innerJoin(engagements, eq(engagements.id, scanRuns.engagementId))
    .innerJoin(organizations, eq(organizations.id, engagements.orgId))
    .where(and(isNotNull(scanRuns.sourcePath), isNotNull(scanRuns.sourcePath)));

  let purged = 0;
  let skippedMonitoring = 0;
  let skippedRecent = 0;

  for (const { scan, engagement, org } of rows) {
    if (!scan.sourcePath) continue;
    const continuous =
      engagement.tier === "CONTINUOUS_MONITORING" || org.plan === "MONITORING";
    if (continuous && !forceAll) {
      skippedMonitoring += 1;
      continue;
    }
    let mtime: Date;
    try {
      const stat = await fs.stat(scan.sourcePath);
      mtime = stat.mtime;
    } catch {
      // Source already gone; mark it purged so the UI reflects reality.
      await db
        .update(scanRuns)
        .set({ sourcePath: null, sourcePurgedAt: new Date() })
        .where(eq(scanRuns.id, scan.id));
      continue;
    }
    if (mtime.getTime() > cutoff) {
      skippedRecent += 1;
      continue;
    }

    await purgeSource(scan.sourcePath);
    await db
      .update(scanRuns)
      .set({ sourcePath: null, sourcePurgedAt: new Date() })
      .where(eq(scanRuns.id, scan.id));
    await db.insert(auditLogs).values({
      action: "source.retention_purged",
      orgId: org.id,
      engagementId: engagement.id,
      detail: {
        scanId: scan.id,
        sequence: scan.sequence,
        retentionDays: days,
        sourceMtime: mtime.toISOString(),
      },
    });
    purged += 1;
  }

  console.log(
    `Retention run complete: ${purged} purged, ${skippedRecent} inside ${days}-day window, ${skippedMonitoring} monitoring snapshots preserved${
      forceAll ? " (force-all)" : ""
    }.`,
  );
}

main()
  .then(async () => {
    await db.$client.end();
  })
  .catch(async (error) => {
    console.error(error);
    await db.$client.end().catch(() => undefined);
    process.exitCode = 1;
  });

async function main() {
  const days = Number.parseInt(

    10,

  if (!Number.isFinite(days) || days < 0) {
    throw new Error("SOURCE_RETENTION_DAYS must be a non-negative number");
  }
  const forceAll = process.argv.includes("--all");
  const cutoff = Date.now() - days * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

  const rows = await db
    .select({
      scan: scanRuns,
      engagement: engagements,
      org: organizations,
    })
    .from(scanRuns)
    .innerJoin(engagements, eq(engagements.id, scanRuns.engagementId))
    .innerJoin(organizations, eq(organizations.id, engagements.orgId))
    .where(and(isNotNull(scanRuns.sourcePath), isNotNull(scanRuns.sourcePath)));

  let purged = 0;
  let skippedMonitoring = 0;
  let skippedRecent = 0;

  for (const { scan, engagement, org } of rows) {
    if (!scan.sourcePath) continue;
    const continuous =
      engagement.tier === "CONTINUOUS_MONITORING" || org.plan === "MONITORING";
    if (continuous && !forceAll) {
      skippedMonitoring += 1;
      continue;
    }
    let mtime: Date;
    try {
      const stat = await fs.stat(scan.sourcePath);
      mtime = stat.mtime;
    } catch {
      // Source already gone; mark it purged so the UI reflects reality.
      await db
        .update(scanRuns)
        .set({ sourcePath: null, sourcePurgedAt: new Date() })
        .where(eq(scanRuns.id, scan.id));
      continue;
    }
    if (mtime.getTime() > cutoff) {
      skippedRecent += 1;
      continue;
    }

    await purgeSource(scan.sourcePath);
    await db
      .update(scanRuns)
      .set({ sourcePath: null, sourcePurgedAt: new Date() })
      .where(eq(scanRuns.id, scan.id));

      orgId: org.id,
      engagementId: engagement.id,
      detail: {
        scanId: scan.id,
        sequence: scan.sequence,
        retentionDays: days,
        sourceMtime: mtime.toISOString(),
      },
    });

type Attempt = { count: number; resetAt: number };

const attempts = new Map<string, Attempt>();
const WINDOW_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000;
const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8;

export function getLoginRateLimit(key: string): {
  allowed: boolean;
  retryAfter?: number;
} {
  const now = Date.now();
  const entry = attempts.get(key);
  if (!entry || entry.resetAt <= now) return { allowed: true };
  if (entry.count >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
    return {
      allowed: false,
      retryAfter: Math.ceil((entry.resetAt - now) / 1000),
    };
  }
  return { allowed: true };
}

export function recordLoginFailure(key: string): void {
  const now = Date.now();
  const entry = attempts.get(key);
  if (!entry || entry.resetAt <= now) {
    attempts.set(key, { count: 1, resetAt: now + WINDOW_MS });
    return;
  }
  entry.count += 1;
}

export function clearLoginAttempts(key: string): void {
  attempts.delete(key);
}

VibeCheck is a single Next.js application backed by PostgreSQL. It covers the whole
service path: client intake, source ingestion, automated scanning, the analyst review
gate, immutable report versions, the client portal, remediation tracking, re-scan
comparison, simulated billing, and the audit trail.

The design constraint behind most decisions: **the platform is the delivery mechanism for
a human service, so every automated result passes through an analyst before a client sees
it.** The gate is enforced in server code, not by hiding buttons.

## Stack

| Layer | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Framework | Next.js 16 (App Router, React Server Components, Server Actions) |
| Language | TypeScript, strict mode |
| Database | PostgreSQL via `drizzle-orm` + `postgres` (node-postgres-style driver) |
| Validation | `zod` at action boundaries |
| Scanning | In-process TypeScript engine combining static rules, secret patterns, and a small dependency advisory database |
| ZIP handling | `fflate` (in-memory extraction with path and size guards) |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS v4, custom design tokens in `src/app/globals.css` |
| Tests | Vitest (`tests/`) |
| Auth | First-party session cookies (SHA-256-hashed tokens in `sessions`) |

No external services are required beyond PostgreSQL. There is no object store, queue,
email provider, or payment p [… 11,643 characters omitted] ult 30) by filesystem mtime, then nulls `sourcePath` and sets `sourcePurgedAt`.
Continuous-monitoring engagements and monitoring-plan orgs are skipped unless `--all` is
passed. Purging is logged. A purged scan cannot be re-run; the client must upload again.
The report and its findings remain.

## Billing (simulated)

`src/lib/billing.ts` mirrors a Stripe Checkout + webhook outcome without Stripe: it
creates a paid invoice, and for monitoring creates or extends a subscription, flips
`organizations.plan` to `MONITORING`, and logs the event. Prices live in
`src/lib/domain.ts` ($399 Quick Scan, $2,500 Full Audit, $499/month monitoring). Swapping
in a real provider means replacing this module and verifying webhooks — no schema change.

## Failure handling

- Ingestion failures surface as form errors with actionable messages; no partial
  engagement is left behind.
- Scan exceptions set `scan_runs.status = FAILED`, store a truncated error, set the
  engagement to `SCAN_FAILED`, and log `scan.failed`.
- A second scan cannot start while one is queued or running for the same engagement.
- Report pages fall back to rebuilding the payload from confirmed findings if the stored
  JSON is missing, rather than showing an empty report.
- `/api/health` checks the database and returns non-200 when it is unreachable.

## Local development

```bash
npm install
createdb vibecheck
cp .env.example .env.local
npm run db:push
npm run db:seed
npm run dev
```

Environment variables: `DATABASE_URL`, `SESSION_SECRET`, optional
`SOURCE_RETENTION_DAYS`, `BILLING_MODE`. The app reads `.env.local` through Next.js.

## Extension points

- **Async scanning:** move `runScan()` behind a job runner; `scan_runs.status` already
  models queued/running/succeeded/failed and the UI polls while active.
- **Real source control:** add a GitHub App with per-installation tokens; keep the clone
  guard as the last line of defense.
- **Payments:** replace `runSimulatedCheckout()` with a provider adapter and idempotent
  webhook handling keyed on `providerRef`.
- **More rules:** add to `customRules`/`secretRules` with a fixture in
  `benchmarks/vulnerable-app` and a clean-case assertion; the benchmark enforces coverage.
- **Multi-analyst workflow:** add assignment and reviewer separation; the audit log
  already records who decided what.

This is the operating procedure for the review desk. It assumes you are signed in as
`ANALYST` or `ADMIN`. The workflow is enforced by the application; where the UI and this
document disagree, the server-side gate wins and this document should be corrected.

## The rule that matters

Nothing reaches a client without a human decision on every finding. The platform will not
let you finalize a report while any finding is `OPEN`, and every triage action clears your
sign-off. Treat the queue as a work list, not a suggestion list.

## 1. Start of shift

Open `/analyst`. The queue shows every engagement with work outstanding, grouped by
urgency:

- **Scan running** — the automated pass is in progress. No action; the page refreshes
  itself. If it stays here for more than a few minutes, see Troubleshooting.
- **Needs review** (`UNDER_REVIEW`) — a completed scan and a draft report. This is your
  queue.
- **Ready for client** (`READY_FOR_CLIENT`) — signed off and finalized, waiting for the
  client to accept terms. No action unless the client asks for changes.
- **Delivered / remediation** — client-owned. Only intervene on a re-scan or a support
  request.

Check the oldest first. Quick Scan carries a 48-hour turnaround; Full Audit carries five
business days; Continuous Monitoring is priority. The engagement header shows the tier
and due expectations.

## 2.  [… 8,702 characters omitted] ion or a clean bill of health.

## 8. Pre-delivery checklist

- [ ] Every finding has a decision; gate reads 100%.
- [ ] At least one critical/high finding has a specific, code-referenced comment.
- [ ] Priorities are set for confirmed findings (P0–P3).
- [ ] Overrides read naturally and do not contradict the snippet.
- [ ] Executive summary names the top risks and the scope.
- [ ] Sign-off note records assumptions and limitations.
- [ ] Report finalized; engagement is `READY_FOR_CLIENT`.
- [ ] Client knows they must accept terms to unlock the report.

## 9. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Engagement stuck in `SCANNING` | Scan process died or the server restarted mid-scan | Check server logs; the scan row may be `RUNNING`. A new scan is blocked while one is active. Operator may need to fail the run in the database, then request a re-scan. |
| `SCAN_FAILED` | Ingestion or engine error | Read the error on the scan record and the `scan.failed` audit entry. Common causes: archive limits, invalid repo URL, private repo, empty source. |
| Finalize button missing | Triage incomplete, no sign-off, or report already final | Check the gate reasons in the finalization panel. |
| Finalize rejected by the server | A decision changed after sign-off, or a scan finished after you loaded the page | Reload; re-sign off if needed. The gate is authoritative. |
| No draft report | Scan did not succeed, or report payload was pruned | The report page rebuilds from confirmed findings when possible; otherwise request a re-scan. |
| Re-scan rejected | Terms not accepted, no successful scan, source purged, or a scan already active | The action returns a specific message; resolve that condition. |
| Client cannot see the report | Not `FINAL`, terms not accepted, or different org | Verify status, `termsAcceptedAt`, and org on the engagement. |
| Cannot access an engagement | Wrong role or wrong tenant | Staff see all; clients see only their org. |

## 10. Audit expectations

Every triage decision, sign-off, finalization, scan, terms acceptance, billing event, and
source purge is written to `audit_logs` with actor, role, org, engagement, and detail.
Assume your actions are attributable. The admin audit log is the record of what happened;
if an action is not in it, the application did not perform it.

export async function addFindingAction(formData: FormData): Promise<void> {
  const analyst = await requireStaff();
  const engagementId = field(formData, "engagementId", 64);
  const title = field(formData, "title", 240);
  const severityRaw = field(formData, "severity", 20) as Severity;
  const owaspRaw = field(formData, "owasp", 10);
  const category = field(formData, "category", 120) || "Analyst observation";
  const filePath = field(formData, "filePath", 400) || "manual-review";
  const lineStart = Math.max(
    1,
    Number.parseInt(field(formData, "lineStart", 10) || "1", 10) || 1,
  );
  const lineEnd = Math.max(
    lineStart,
    Number.parseInt(field(formData, "lineEnd", 10) || String(lineStart), 10) ||
      lineStart,
  );
  const description = field(formData, "description", 4000);
  const remediation = field(formData, "remediation", 4000);
  const comment = field(formData, "comment", 2000);
  const priorityRaw = field(formData, "priority", 10);
  const priority = ["P0", "P1", "P2", "P3"].includes(priorityRaw)
    ? priorityRaw
    : null;
  const back = backTo(engagementId);

  if (title.length < 5) redirectWithError(back, "Add a descriptive finding title.");
  if (!SEVERITY_ORDER.includes(severityRaw)) {
    redirectWithError(back, "Choose a valid severity.");
  }
  if (description.length < 10) {
    redirectWithError(back, "Describe the issue and its impact.");
  }
  if (remediation.length < 10) {
    redirectWithError(back, "Add remediation guidance.");
  }
  const owasp = owaspRaw in OWASP_CATEGORIES ? owaspRaw : "A04";

  const [engagement] = await db
    .select()
    .from(engagements)
    .where(eq(engagements.id, engagementId))
    .limit(1);
  if (!engagement) redirectWithError("/analyst", "Engagement not found.");

  const [scan] = await db
    .select()
    .from(scanRuns)
    .where(eq(scanRuns.engagementId, engagementId))
    .orderBy(desc(scanRuns.sequence))
    .limit(1);
  if (!scan) redirectWithError(back, "Run a scan before adding findings.");
  const [report] = await db
    .select({ status: reports.status })
    .from(reports)
    .where(eq(reports.scanId, scan.id))
    .orderBy(desc(reports.version))
    .limit(1);
  if (report?.status === "FINAL") {
    redirectWithError(back, "The report is already finalized.");
  }

  const now = new Date();
  await db.insert(findings).values({

  await resetReviewSignoff(engagementId);

{"kind":"tool","id":"dvFxxP-hfes","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"docs/client-help.md","instructions":"Write client-facing portal help documentation.","content":"# Client help

This guide covers the client portal: submitting an audit, tracking it through review,
reading the report, tracking remediation, and requesting a re-scan.

> **Prototype notice.** This workspace is a working demo, not a live commercial service.
> Billing is simulated, emails are not sent, and the service terms are placeholders. See
> [prototype scope](prototype-scope.md).

## What the service does

You submit a repository snapshot. VibeCheck runs an automated static review (OWASP-mapped
rules, secrets, dependency and license risk, and AI-code/MCP-specific checks), then a
human analyst validates **every** finding, removes false positives, and writes the
client-facing commentary. You receive an immutable, versioned report plus a remediation
tracker. A re-scan verifies what changed.

The review is static. It does not include penetration testing, exploitation, runtime
monitoring, or a review of infrastructure outside the submitted code.

## Signing in

Open `/login` and use the credentials provided for your organization. In the demo build,
the login page lists the sample accounts and fills them in when clicked:

| Role | Email | Password |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Client (Acme) | `client@acme.dev` | `Client123!` |
| Client (Northwind) | `client@northwind.dev` | `Client123!` |
| Analyst | `analyst@vibecheck.dev` | `Analyst123!` |
| Operator | `admin@vibechec [… 6,310 characters omitted] analyst review.

You will not see the new report until the analyst triages the new findings, signs off, and
finalizes it. Prior analyst decisions carry forward, so a re-scan does not repeat the
whole review — but new code still gets human review.

## Billing

`/portal/billing` shows your plan, subscription status, renewal date, and invoice ledger.
In this prototype:

- Starting an audit creates a **simulated paid invoice** — no card is charged.
- Continuous Monitoring creates or extends a simulated monthly subscription and upgrades
  the organization plan.
- Upgrading is a test-mode action; the interface mirrors what a real checkout callback
  would do.

Do not enter real payment details anywhere in this build; there is no payment form and no
provider connected.

## Data handling and retention

- Source is stored under a managed directory outside the web root, accessible only to
  staff through the application.
- Secrets are redacted from stored snippets and report output. This is a safety net, not a
  substitute for rotation.
- Access is logged: report views, terms acceptance, remediation changes, scans, and
  billing events.
- Source snapshots are purged after the retention window (default 30 days) by an operator
  job; continuous-monitoring engagements are exempt so future re-scans can run. Purged
  scans keep their findings and reports.
- Source is not used to train models.

## FAQ

**Can I see the report before the analyst finishes?** No. Drafts are staff-only, and the
client route returns not-found rather than a preview.

**Why is a finding I expected missing?** It may have been dismissed as a false positive
(dismissals are not shown), or the scan may not have covered that file type or path. Check
the scope section and ask your analyst.

**Why does the score differ from a tool like Snyk?** Different weighting, different rule
set, and a human removed false positives. Use the finding list and priorities for
decisions, not the number alone.

**Can I get the raw JSON?** The report payload is stored server-side for each version. Ask
the operator; the UI renders the report rather than exposing the raw payload.

**Who do I contact?** In the demo, use the analyst account or the operator account listed
on the login page. A production deployment would wire support and notification channels.

This repository is a working end-to-end prototype built against the PRD. It is not a
production service. This page separates what is real from what is simulated, so nobody
mistakes the demo for a shippable security product.

## What is genuinely implemented

- **Tenant model and access control.** Organizations, users, roles, hashed session
  cookies, server-side role guards, and org-scoped queries. Clients cannot read another
  tenant's engagement or report, and drafts are hidden from clients.
- **Intake.** Create an engagement from a demo repository, a ZIP upload, or a public
  GitHub/GitLab clone, with tier selection and intake context. Ingestion enforces archive
  size, file-count, path-traversal, and repository-URL guards.
- **Scanning engine.** 29 rule IDs across AI-code patterns, MCP server risks, secret
  families, known vulnerable dependencies, and restrictive licenses. Fingerprints exclude
  line numbers; secret values are redacted before persistence.
- **Review gate.** A server-enforced finalization gate: successful scan, every finding
  decided, explicit analyst sign-off, draft report. Any triage change resets sign-off.
- **Immutable report versions.** Finalization freezes a JSON payload built from confirmed
  findings; a re-scan produces a new draft version. Reports render for staff and clients
  with methodolog [… 6,099 characters omitted] emented: scrypt password hashing, hashed session tokens, httpOnly cookies, server-side
authorization on pages and actions, org scoping, input length limits, ZIP traversal guards,
repository allowlisting, subprocess timeouts, secret redaction, and an append-only audit
trail by convention.

Known weaknesses that must be fixed before exposure to real client code:

1. Demo credentials and a committed dev `SESSION_SECRET` default.
2. No MFA/SSO, no password reset, no session revocation UI.
3. No security headers/CSP; no CSRF token beyond `SameSite=Lax` and Next.js action origin
   checks.
4. In-memory rate limiting that resets on restart and is per-process.
5. No encryption at rest beyond the database/host defaults; source sits on local disk.
6. No malware scanning of uploaded archives and no sandbox around the scanner.
7. No tenant-level audit export or anomaly detection.
8. Error messages can include upstream git output; review before exposing.

## Suggested path to production

1. **Harden identity:** managed auth or SSO + MFA, invites, reset, session revocation,
   shared rate limiting, security headers.
2. **Move scanning off the request path:** durable queue, worker isolation, resource
   limits, retries, crash recovery, per-tenant concurrency.
3. **Move source to object storage:** encryption, short-lived signed access, per-tenant
   prefixes, lifecycle rules aligned with retention.
4. **Connect the real supply chain:** live advisory feeds, SBOM generation, lockfile
   coverage, private repo integration via a GitHub App.
5. **Add delivery automation:** transactional email, PDF generation and archival,
   notification preferences.
6. **Replace billing:** provider checkout, verified webhooks, idempotency, entitlements,
   tax/refunds.
7. **Operate it:** structured logs, metrics, tracing, alerting, backups/PITR, restore
   drills, on-call runbook.
8. **Legal and compliance:** counsel-reviewed terms, DPA, privacy policy, retention
   schedule, incident response, and a security review of the platform itself.
9. **Prove quality:** a labeled corpus with measured precision/recall per rule family,
   regression gates in CI, and an E2E suite for the delivery workflow.

Until those are done, treat this as a demonstration of the service model and workflow —
not a system to point at a client's real repository.

# VibeCheck — Productized AI-Code Security Audit Platform

Here's a complete walkthrough of all features, one by one, with code-backed examples.

---

## 1. Role-Based Access Control

The platform has three roles scoped to organizations, enforced server-side on every page and action.

### How it works

- **ADMIN** — can view all engagements, clients, audit logs; can finalize reports.
- **ANALYST** — sees the review queue, can triage findings, sign off, finalize reports.
- **CLIENT** — only sees their own organization's engagements and reports; terms-gated.

### Code example

```tsx
// src/lib/permissions.ts — server-side check
export function canAccessClientReport(
  user: Pick<SessionUser, "role" | "orgId">,
  engagement: { orgId: string },
  report: { status: string },
  termsAcceptedAt: Date | null,
): boolean {
  if (!canViewEngagement(user, engagement)) return false;  // org scoping
  if (isStaff(user)) return true;                         // staff sees everything
  return report.status === "FINAL" && Boolean(termsAcceptedAt);  // client gate
}
```

**Result**: If a client tries `/analyst/engagements/f26ce171`, they get redirected to `/login`. If they forge a URL to another org's report, they get a 404.

### Demo accounts

| Role | Email | Password | Sees |
|------|-------|----------|------|
| Analyst | `analyst@vibecheck.dev` | `Analyst123!` | Review queue, triage desk, ruleset, reports |
| Client (Acme) | `client@acme.dev` | `Client123!` | Delivered audit, remediation tracker, billing |
| Admin (operator) | `admin@vibecheck.dev` | `Admin123!` | All engagements, clients, audit log |

---

## 2. Client Portal — Intake & Dashboard

The client enters the service through `/portal/new`, a 4-step form that records the engagement and kicks off scanning.

### Step 1 — Engagement name

A human-readable name (e.g., "Acme payments API — pre-launch") that appears on the engagement list.

### Step 2 — Audit tier

| Tier | Price | Turnaround | Includes |
|------|-------|------------|----------|
| QUICK_SCAN | $399 | 48 hours | OWASP scan, AI-code + secrets + dependency checks, analyst validation, client-ready report |
| FULL_AUDIT | $2,500 | 5 business days | Quick Scan + full analyst triage + prioritized remediation plan + one verification re-scan + report version history |
| CONTINUOUS_MONITORING | $499/month | Priority queue | Recurring scheduled re-scans + PR-triggered checks (Phase 2) + priority analyst turnaround + risk trend tracking |

### Step 3 — Source (3 modes)

| Mode | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| **SAMPLE** | Copies `benchmarks/vulnerable-app` (demo only) |
| **ZIP** | Upload ≤25 MB; extracts to ≤40 MB / ≤3,000 files, skipping `node_modules`, `.git`, traversal paths |
| **GITHUB** | `git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --no-tags` of a public HTTPS repo; private repos rejected |

**ZIP guards** (in `src/lib/ingest.ts`):
- Valid ZIP signature (`0x50 0x4b`)
- 25 MB upload cap
- 40 MB extracted cap
- 5 MB per-file limit
- 3,000 entry cap
- Rejection of absolute paths and `..` traversal
- Skipping `node_modules/`, `.git/`, `.next/`, `__MACOSX/`, `.DS_Store`

**Repository guard**: HTTPS only, no credentials in URL, host allowlist (`github.com`, `gitlab.com`), exactly `owner/repo` path, no query/hash, 120-second timeout.

### Step 4 — Intake context

Stack, deployment target, compliance drivers, and free-text notes the analyst should know.

### Dashboard (portal)

Shows the engagement list with status, risk score, and scan metadata. Clients see only their org's engagements.

---

## 3. Analyst Desk — Review Queue

The analyst's workspace at `/analyst` shows every engagement needing decisions.

### Queue summary panel

- **Percent triaged** — progress bar; green when 100%.
- **Open / total** — count of `OPEN` findings.
- **Confirmed / dismissed** — quality metrics.
- **Review gate** — "Signed off" or "Not signed off" with timestamp.

### Per-engagement view

Each engagement card shows:
- Tier and source type
- Risk score + grade (e.g., "100 / F")
- Severity breakdown
- Scan stats (files scanned, duration)
- Auto-refresh indicator

### Triage actions on each finding

For every finding, the analyst chooses one outcome:

| Action | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| **Confirm** | Marks `analystStatus = "CONFIRMED"`. Sets priority (P0–P3), writes analyst comment (client-facing), optionally edits title/description/remediation (client-facing copy override). |
| **Dismiss / false positive** | Marks `analystStatus = "DISMISSED"`. Writes a one-line reason in the comment. Counts toward the false-positive rate. |
| **Reopen** | If inheriting a decided finding and disagreeing; resets sign-off like any triage change. |
| **Bulk confirm** | Confirms every `OPEN` finding at or above a confidence threshold (50–95%) in one action. Still requires subsequent sign-off. |
| **Add analyst finding** | Records a manual observation — architecture issues, design gaps, MCP trust-boundary problems, secrets‑management flaws. Tagged as `source: "ANALYST"` and survive re-scans. |

**Example**: Finding `AI-CRED-001` with severity `CRITICAL` — the analyst confirms it, sets priority `P0 — now`, writes comment "Hardcoded SendGrid API key in config.js, line 42; rotate immediately", and leaves the generated snippet untouched since it's already redacted.

---

## 4. Review Gate — Hard Requirement

FR-10: **No report reaches a client without analyst review.** The gate runs server-side on finalization and cannot be bypassed by the UI.

### `canFinalizeReport()` in `src/lib/review.ts`

```ts
export function canFinalizeReport({
  findings,
  reviewCompletedAt,
  reportStatus,
  hasScan,
}: FinalizeGateInput): FinalizeGateResult {
  const reasons: string[] = [];
  if (!hasScan) reasons.push("The engagement has no completed scan.");
  if (!reviewCompletedAt) reasons.push("Analyst review has not been completed.");
  if (reportStatus !== "DRAFT") reasons.push("There is no draft report to finalize.");
  const state = getReviewState(findings);
  if (!state.triageComplete) {
    reasons.push(
      `${state.open} finding${state.open === 1 ? "" : "s"} still need an analyst decision.`,
    );
  }
  return { ok: reasons.length === 0, reasons };
}
```

**Gate conditions** (all must pass):
1. Engagement has a successful scan.
2. `reviewCompletedAt` is set (analyst sign-off).
3. A draft report exists.
4. Zero findings are `OPEN` — every finding is `CONFIRMED` or `DISMISSED`.

**Critical**: Any triage action (`confirm`, `dismiss`, `reopen`, `bulk confirm`) calls `resetReviewSignoff()`, which clears the sign-off timestamp. The analyst must sign off again after changing any decision.

---

## 5. Report Finalization & Immutable Delivery

When the gate passes, the analyst presses **Finalize report vN**. The server:

1. Re-runs the gate (authoritative).
2. Builds the payload from **confirmed findings only** (dismissed and analyst-added findings are excluded from the client-visible set).
3. Marks the report `FINAL` and moves the engagement to `READY_FOR_CLIENT`.
4. Logs `report.finalized` in the audit trail.
5. Further triage is disabled for that scan — corrections require a new scan and a new report version.

### Report payload structure (PR §13.9 deliverable)

```ts
export interface ReportPayload {
  schemaVersion: 1;
  version: number;
  generatedAt: string;
  executiveSummary: string;     // analyst's framing
  engagement: { id, name, tier, tierLabel, repoUrl, sourceType, createdAt };
  organization: { name: string };
  scan: {
    id, sequence, finishedAt, filesScanned, engineVersion, durationMs;
    score: number;           // 0–100, higher is worse
    grade: string;          // A–F
    counts: SeverityCounts; // CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/INFO
    comparison: ScanComparison | null; // re-scan diff
  };
  findings: ReportFindingSnapshot[]; // redacted snippets, no raw secrets
  counts: SeverityCounts;
  score: number;
  grade: string;
  analystNote: string | null;     // from sign-off note
  methodology: string[];         // what was scanned
  limitations: string[];         // scope limitations
  disclaimer: string;            // not a certification
}
```

### What the client sees

- Engagement metadata (tier, files scanned, engine version)
- Executive summary (headline risk + top fixes + caveats)
- Risk score + grade (A–F)
- Severity counts
- Findings with: severity, OWASP category, source family (AI-code/secret/SCA/license/analyst), file & line, **redacted** snippet, description, remediation, priority
- Analyst note (scope assumptions, limitations)
- Methodology and limitations sections
- Disclaimer (report is not a certification)

**Dismissed findings** are not shown, but the report notes the review-quality metrics. **Analyst-added findings** appear alongside automated ones.

---

## 6. Remediation Tracking

After delivery, the engagement enters `REMEDIATION` mode. The client marks findings from the current report as remediated.

### Marking remediated

- Select **Remediated** on a finding.
- Optional note describing the fix (commit SHA, PR number, change summary).
- `clientStatus` flips from `OPEN` to `REMEDIATED`; `remediatedAt` is set.
- If it's the first finding marked remediated and the engagement was `DELIVERED`, the status switches to `REMEDIATION`.

### Re-scan verification

> The re-scan is the verification step. Marking a finding remediated is an assertion, not proof.

When the client requests a re-scan:
- Uses the **retained snapshot** (not the local working copy).
- Runs the engine against the snapshot.
- Compares by stable fingerprint (not line numbers).
- Marks previously confirmed findings that disappeared as **RESOLVED** (counted in comparison).
- Shows new, outstanding, and resolved counts plus score delta.
- Creates a new draft report version; engagement returns to `UNDER_REVIEW`.

**Example**: Scan 1 had a `AI-SQL-001` finding on `routes/api/users.ts:15`. After the client fixes the query to use parameterized DB calls, a re-scan finds the fingerprint no longer matches → the finding is marked `RESOLVED` in the comparison, and the score drops.

If the source was purged by retention (default 30 days), the re-scan cannot run — the client must upload a fresh snapshot.

---

## 7. Scanning Engine — 29 Named Checks

The engine combines multiple rule families across the retained snapshot.

### AI-code rules (18 checks)

Target patterns common in LLM/Vibe-coded output:

| ID | Pattern |
|----|---------|
| AI-SQL-001 | String-concatenated database queries |
| AI-AUTH-001 | Missing object-level authorization on generated CRUD endpoints |
| AI-CRED-001 | Hardcoded default credentials or API keys |
| AI-CORS-001 | Overly permissive CORS configuration |
| AI-JWT-001 | Unverified JWT payload usage |
| AI-RAND-001 | `Math.random()` used for token generation |
| AI-HASH-001 | Weak hashing (MD5, SHA1) for secrets |
| AI-EVAL-001 | `eval()` usage |
| AI-UPLOAD-001 | Unrestricted file uploads |
| AI-SSRF-001 | User-controlled `fetch()` URLs (SSRF) |
| AI-MASS-001 | Mass assignment on generated models |
| AI-RATE-001 | Missing rate limits on auth endpoints |
| AI-DEBUG-001 | Debug mode left in production code |
| AI-RLS-001 | Missing Postgres RLS policies |
| AI-TLS-001 | Disabled TLS verification |
| AI-IAM-001 | Wildcard IAM permissions |
| AI-XSS-001 | Unvalidated HTML injection |
| AI-REDIR-001 | Unvalidated redirect targets |

### MCP server rules (3 checks)

| ID | Pattern |
|----|---------|
| MCP-AUTH-001 | Missing authentication on MCP tool endpoints |
| MCP-PERM-001 | Overly broad tool permissions |
| MCP-CMD-001 | Shell execution from tool arguments |

### Secrets detection (6 checks)

| ID | Pattern |
|----|---------|
| Cloud provider keys (AWS, GCP, Azure) |
| Payment keys (Stripe, PayPal) |
| SaaS API tokens (Slack, GitHub) |
| Private keys (PEM-formatted) |
| Database URLs with embedded credentials |
| Generic high-entropy assignments |

### SCA / License (2 checks)

- Parses `package.json`, lockfiles; matches ~12 known-vulnerable package ranges.
- Flags restrictive licenses (copyleft/source-available) in direct and vendored manifests.

**Fingerprint**: `sha256(ruleId + filePath + normalized evidence)[:32]`. Line numbers excluded so unrelated edits don't make every finding look new. Secret evidence is hashed rather than stored.

### Example finding

```
ruleId: "AI-CRED-001"
source: "CRED"
title: "Hardcoded credential in config.js"
severity: "CRITICAL"
owasp: "A02: Cryptographic Failures"
category: "SECRET"
filePath: "config.js"
lineStart: 42
lineEnd: 42
snippet: "[REDACTED — secret was in this assignment]"
description: "A secret matching the AWS key pattern was found in config.js line 42."
remediation: "Rotate the credential immediately. Use an environment variable or secret manager."
confidence: 95
fingerprint: "a1b2c3d4e5f6..."  // stable across line reflows
```

## 8. Audit Trail

Every action is written append-only:

```
engagement.created, engagement.viewed, engagement.closed,
scan.queued, scan.completed, scan.failed,
scan.rescan_requested,
finding.confirmed, finding.bulk_confirmed,
finding.added,
report.finalized,
review.completed,
terms.accepted,
billing.simulated_checkout,
billing.subscription_upgraded,

```

Each entry has: actor, actor role, actor email, orgId, engagementId, action, detail JSON, timestamp.

The admin audit-log page (`/admin/audit-log`) renders this trail. The append-only convention means the database does not enforce immutability, but the application never writes update/delete paths.

---

## 9. Source Retention

Retained snapshots live under `.data/sources/<engagementId>/<scanId>/repo`. They exist for:
- Analyst review (browsing the code that was scanned).
- Re-scan comparison (running the engine again against the same code).
- Audit trail (knowing what code was reviewed).

`scripts/purge-sources.ts` deletes snapshots older than `SOURCE_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 30). Continuous-monitoring engagements and monitoring-plan orgs are skipped unless `--all` is passed. Purging is logged; a purged scan cannot be re-run — the client must upload again. The report and its findings remain.

```
        │
        ▼
scan engine (29 rules) → findings + risk score
        │
        ▼
ANALYST GATE (server-enforced):
  • every finding decided (confirm/dismiss)
  • explicit sign-off
  • draft report exists
  ▼
canFinalizeReport() passes → FINAL report + READY_FOR_CLIENT
        │
        ▼
client accepts terms → report unlocks
        │
        ▼
remediation tracker (mark findings remediated)
        │
        ▼
request re-scan → retained snapshot → comparison
  • resolved / new / outstanding + score delta
  • new draft report → analyst review again
        │
        ▼
close / upgrade to Continuous Monitoring
```

Everything is scoped by `orgId`, enforced server-side, and nothing reaches a client without the analyst gate. The platform is the delivery mechanism for a human service — the scan engine buys breadth, the analyst judgment buys trust.

{"kind":"tool","id":"dxBR0gjciUI","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"docs/user-manual.md","instructions":"Write a simple user manual for the VibeCheck product, explaining how clients and analysts use it day to day.","content":"# VibeCheck User Manual

Welcome to VibeCheck — a security audit service for teams shipping AI-generated code. This manual shows you how to use the platform day to day.

## Table of Contents
1. [Signing In](#signing-in)
2. [Starting a New Audit (Clients)](#starting-a-new-audit-clients)
3. [The Review Queue (Analysts)](#the-review-queue-analysts)
4. [Viewing Your Report](#viewing-your-report-clients)
5. [Accepting Terms & Unlocking the Report](#accepting-terms--unlocking-the-report)
6. [Marking Findings as Remediated](#marking-findings-as-remediated)
7. [Requesting a Re‑Scan](#requesting-a-rescan)
8. [Billing & Subscription (Simulated)](#billing--subscription-simulated)
9. [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

---

## 1. Signing In

Open the app at `http://localhost:3210/login`.

You'll see demo accounts on the page. Click the button for your role, or fill in your own email/password:

| Role | Email | Password | What you can do |
|------|-------|----------|-----------------|
| **Analyst** | `analyst@vibecheck.dev` | `Analyst123!` | Triage findings, sign off reports, finalize audits |
| **Client (Acme)** | `client@acme.dev` | `Client123!` | View delivered audits, mark remediation, request re‑scans |
| **Admin (operator)** | `admin@vibecheck.dev` | `Admin123!` | See all engagements, clients, audit log |

> **Note**: These are prototype accounts. In a production deployment, you would sign up through your organization's invite system.

After signing in, you're routed to the page that matches your role.

---

## 2. Starting a New Audit (Clients)

Only clients can start new audits. From the dashboard (`/portal`), click **New audit**.

### The 4-step intake form

| Step | What you do |
|------|-------------|
| **1. Engagement name** | Give it a recognizable name, e.g., "Acme payments API — pre‑launch". |
| **2. Audit tier** | Choose one: |
| | • **Quick Scan** ($399) — fast, 48‑hour turnaround. Covers OWASP checks, AI‑code patterns, secrets, and dependencies. An analyst gives every finding a decision. |
| | • **Full Audit** ($2,500) — includes everything in Quick Scan plus a deep analyst triage, prioritized remediation plan, and one verification re‑scan. Turnaround: ~5 business days. |
| | • **Continuous Monitoring** ($499/month) — scheduled re‑scans and PR‑triggered checks going forward. You'll get a monthly invoice. |
| **3. Source** | Pick how you give us code to review: |
| | • **Demo repo** — use the built‑in sample (good for trying the product). |
| | • **Upload .zip** — drag a repository zip (max 25 MB, expands to max 40 MB with up to 3,000 files). Do **not** include `node_modules`, `.git`, or secrets you haven't rotated. |
| | • **Public repo** — paste a public GitHub/GitLab URL (`https://github.com/owner/repo`). Private repos are not supported in this prototype. |
| **4. Intake context** (optional) | Add any notes the analyst should know: recent AI‑assisted rewrite, risky areas, launch date, compliance concerns, etc. This helps them prioritize. |

After step 4, the engagement is created and the scan starts automatically. You'll be taken to the engagement page where you can watch the progress.

### What happens after you submit

| Status | Meaning | Your action |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| **Intake** | Submitted, queued | None |
| **Scanning** | Automated pass running | Wait — the page refreshes itself. |
| **Scan failed** | Ingestion or engine error | Check the error message; contact your analyst if you're unsure. |
| **Analyst review** | A human is reviewing every finding | This is the service. No action needed from you. |
| **Ready for client** | Report is finalized, waiting for you | **Accept the terms** (next section). |
| **Delivered** | Report available | Start marking findings remediated or request a re‑scan. |
| **Remediation** | You're fixing findings | Mark progress, then request a re‑scan when ready. |
| **Closed** | Engagement complete | None. |

---

## 3. The Review Queue (Analysts)

If you sign in as the analyst, you see the **review desk** at `/analyst`. This is your work list.

### Queue summary

At the top you see:
- **Percent triaged** — a progress bar. Turns green when you've decided every finding.
- **Open / total** — how many findings still need a decision.
- **Confirmed / dismissed** — quality metrics.
- **Review gate** — "Signed off" or "Not signed off" with the timestamp of when you signed.

### Per-engagement card

Each engagement card shows:
- The tier (Quick Scan, Full Audit, Monitoring).
- Risk score and grade (e.g., "100 / F" means high severity everywhere).
- Severity breakdown (critical, high, medium, low, info).
- Scan stats (files scanned, how long it took).
- An auto‑refresh indicator (the page updates itself while a scan runs).

### Triage each finding

Expand a finding to see the rule, file, line, redacted code snippet, description, and remediation guidance.

For each finding, choose one:

| Button | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| **Confirm finding** | Marks this as a real issue. You can set a priority (P0 — now, P1 — this sprint, P2 — scheduled, P3 — backlog), write an analyst comment (the client will see this), and optionally edit the title/description/remediation that the client sees. |
| **Dismiss / false positive** | Marks this as not a real issue. Write a brief reason in the comment (e.g., "Test fixture, not production code"). This counts toward the false‑positive rate, so be deliberate. |
| **Reopen** | If you inherit a decided finding and disagree, use this to retriage it. Resets sign‑off, so you'll need to sign off again later. |
| **Bulk confirm** (right rail) | Confirm every OPEN finding at or above a confidence threshold (50–95%) in one click. Still requires a subsequent sign‑off. |
| **Add analyst finding** | Use this for issues the static engine can't see — missing authorization on a specific handler, a trust‑boundary crossed without validation, a secrets‑management gap, or a business‑logic flaw. You give it a title, severity, category, file/line, description, remediation, and confidence. This finding will appear in the report and survive re‑scans. |

### Signing off

When every finding has a decision (0 open), the **sign‑off panel** appears in the right rail.

1. **Write a sign‑off note** (optional but recommended). This records your assumptions, caveats, and anything the client must know to read the report correctly. This note becomes the "analyst note" in the final report.
2. Press **Complete analyst review**. The engagement records the sign‑off, logs it in the audit trail, and moves to `UNDER_REVIEW` → `READY_FOR_CLIENT`.

> **Important**: Any later triage change (confirm, dismiss, reopen, bulk confirm) clears the sign‑off. You'll need to sign off again after changing any decision.

### Finalizing the report

After sign‑off, a **finalization panel** appears with a generated executive summary.

1. **Edit the executive summary** if needed. It should stand alone for a non‑technical reader: what was reviewed, the headline risk, the top 2‑3 things to fix first, and the most important caveat. Keep the generated structure if it's accurate; remove boilerplate that doesn't apply.
2. Press **Finalize report vN**. The server builds an immutable payload from confirmed findings only, marks the report `FINAL`, and moves the engagement to `READY_FOR_CLIENT`. This is logged as `report.finalized`.

The report is now immutable. Corrections require a new scan and a new report version — there is no edit path, by design.

---

## 4. Viewing Your Report (Clients)

Once the analyst has finalized the report and the engagement is `READY_FOR_CLIENT`, the report unlocks **only after you accept the service terms**.

### Accepting terms

1. Open the engagement page. You'll see a short terms panel.
2. Read the prototype terms (or open the full terms at `/terms` if you want the complete text).
3. Check the **I accept the service terms** checkbox.
4. Press the unlock button.

Acceptance is recorded with your user, timestamp, and the engagement in the audit log. It's not a per‑report click‑through that can be dismissed — it unlocks delivery for that engagement. If a colleague needs to accept, they must sign in with their own account.

### What the report contains

When the report opens, you'll see:

- **Engagement & scope** — what was reviewed, the tier, files scanned, engine version, scan duration. Check this first; a truncated scan limits what the report can tell you.
- **Executive summary** — the analyst's framing of the headline risk and what to fix first. Written for a non‑technical reader.
- **Risk score & grade** — 0–100 (higher is worse) with letter grades A–F. This is a prioritization aid, not a certification.
- **Severity counts** — how many critical, high, medium, low, info findings.
- **Findings** — each with:
  - Severity and OWASP category (e.g., A02: Cryptographic Failures)
  - Source family (AI-code rules, secrets, dependencies, license, or analyst)
  - File path and line number
  - **Redacted** code snippet (raw credentials are never shown)
  - Analyst's explanation of why this matters
  - Remediation guidance (how to fix it)
  - Priority (P0–P3) — your remediation order
- **Analyst note** — scope assumptions and caveats from the sign‑off.
- **Methodology & limitations** — what was and was not tested.
- **Disclaimer** — the report is not a certification or compliance attestation.

### Print-friendly view

Use the **print button** on the report page for a print‑friendly view or to save as PDF via your browser.

### Report version history

The engagement page shows how many report versions exist. Each finalization creates a new version (v1, v2, …). Earlier versions are immutable history; you can't edit them, but you can compare them if you request a re‑scan.

---

## 5. Accepting Terms & Unlocking the Report

This is a one‑time step per engagement.

1. On the engagement page, look for the **terms panel** near the top.
2. Read the short terms (or click **View full terms** to open `/terms`).
3. Check the **I accept** box.
4. The **Unlock report** button becomes active. Click it.

The engagement status changes to `DELIVERED`, and the remediation tracker and re‑scan button appear.

> **Why is this here?** The service terms are a prototype placeholder, not legal advice. In production they would be counsel‑reviewed contracts that a client must accept before receiving a security audit report.

---

## 6. Marking Findings as Remediated

After the report is delivered, the engagement enters the `REMEDIATION` phase. You mark findings that you've fixed.

### How to mark a finding remediated

1. On the engagement page, go to the **Remediation** section (appears after delivery).
2. Find the confirmed finding you fixed.
3. Click **Mark as remediated**.
4. Optionally add a note describing the fix (commit SHA, PR number, change summary).
5. The finding's `clientStatus` flips from `OPEN` to `REMEDIATED`, and `remediatedAt` is set.

### Progress counters

- **Open** — confirmed findings you haven't marked remediated yet.
- **Remediated** — findings you've marked fixed.
- When the first finding is marked remediated and the engagement was `DELIVERED`, the status switches to `REMEDIATION`.

> **Remember**: Marking a finding remediated is your assertion that it's fixed. The **re‑scan** is the verification step. Only findings in the current final report can be tracked; stale findings from older scan versions are read‑only history.

### Requesting a re‑scan when you're done

1. In the Remediation section, click **Request re‑scan**.
2. Requirements (the button is disabled until they're met):
   - You have accepted the terms.
   - There is a final report.
   - The source snapshot is still retained (retention defaults to 30 days; continuous‑monitoring engagements keep it longer).
   - No scan is currently queued or running.
3. The re‑scan runs the engine against the **retained snapshot** — not your local working copy. If you fixed code after uploading, the platform won't see those fixes. For a materially changed codebase, start a new engagement and upload the current code, or ask the operator.
4. When the scan completes, you get a new draft report and a comparison strip showing resolved/new/outstanding findings and the score delta.
5. The engagement returns to `UNDER_REVIEW`. The analyst triages new findings, signs off, and finalizes a new report version. Prior analyst decisions carry forward by fingerprint, so the review doesn't start from scratch — but new code still gets human review.

If the source was purged by retention, the re‑scan cannot run — you must upload a fresh snapshot.

---

## 7. Billing & Subscription (Simulated)

In this prototype, billing doesn't charge real money. It records simulated invoices and subscriptions in the database.

### What you see on `/portal/billing`

- **Current plan** — your tier (NONE, MONITORING, etc.).
- **Invoices** — a ledger of simulated paid invoices.
- **Subscription status** — active, past due, canceled.
- **Audit tiers** — reference prices:
  - Quick Scan: $399 (one‑time)
  - Full Audit: $2,500 (one‑time)
  - Continuous Monitoring: $499/month (recurring)

### Starting an audit creates a simulated invoice

When you create a new engagement, a paid invoice is written to the database with:
- A simulated provider reference (`sim_<uuid>`).
- Status `PAID`.
- No card is charged.

### Upgrading to Continuous Monitoring

If you're on a one‑time tier and want ongoing coverage:
1. Go to **Billing** → **Upgrade subscription**.
2. The interface mirrors a Stripe checkout callback — it creates/extends a monthly subscription and flips your organization plan to `MONITORING`.
3. You'll see a recurring invoice and the platform will allow scheduled re‑scans going forward (Phase 2 connector not yet built in this prototype).

### No real payment details are ever entered

There is no payment form, no provider connection, and no live charges. If you need real billing, replace the `runSimulatedCheckout()` module in `src/lib/billing.ts` with a Stripe integration.

---

## 8. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
|---------|--------------|------------|
| Engagement stuck in **Scanning** | Scan process died or server restarted mid‑scan | Check server logs; the scan row may be `RUNNING`. An operator can fail the run in the database, then you can request a re‑scan. |
| **Scan failed** | Archive too large, invalid repo URL, private repo, empty source | Read the error on the scan record and the `scan.failed` audit entry. Common causes: ZIP limits, invalid repo URL, private repo, empty source. |
| Finalize button **missing** | Triage incomplete, no sign‑off, or report already finalized | Check the gate reasons in the finalization panel. All findings must be decided, sign‑off must be complete, and a draft report must exist. |
| Finalize **rejected by server** | A decision changed after you signed off, or you loaded the page later | Reload the page; re‑sign off if needed. The gate is authoritative. |
| No **draft report** | Scan did not succeed, or report payload was pruned | The report page can rebuild from confirmed findings when possible; otherwise request a re‑scan. |
| Client **cannot see the report** | Report not `FINAL`, terms not accepted, or different org | Verify the report status is `FINAL`, that `termsAcceptedAt` is set on the engagement, and that you're in the correct organization. |
| Cannot **access an engagement** | Wrong role or wrong tenant | Staff (ADMIN/ANALYST) see all; clients see only their own org. If you think you should have access, sign in with the correct account. |
| Re‑scan **rejected** | Terms not accepted, no successful scan, source purged, or a scan already active | The action returns a specific message; resolve that condition first. |
| **Terms checkbox** doesn't unlock the report | You may be on a different org's engagement, or the report isn't finalized | Verify you're on your own org's engagement and the report status is `FINAL`. |
| **Important**: raw secret in snippet | The redaction layer may miss some patterns | Rotate the credential immediately. The redaction is a safety net, not a substitute for rotation. Mention it in the intake notes so the analyst can prioritize it. |

---

## Quick‑Start Recap

| Role | What you do first |
|------|-------------------|
| **Client** | Sign in → **New audit** → pick tier & source → fill intake → wait for scan → accept terms → read report → mark remediation / request re‑scan |
| **Analyst** | Sign in → review queue → triage every finding → sign off → finalize report → client accepts terms → monitor remediation / re‑scans |
| **Admin** | Sign in → overview of all engagements → operator actions (purge sources, close engagements, view audit log) |

---

## Need Help?

- In the demo, the analyst (`analyst@vibecheck.dev`) and operator (`admin@vibecheck.dev`) accounts are the primary support contacts.
- For production deployments, the platform would include a support ticket form, email notifications, and a status page.
- All actions are logged in the **audit log** (`/admin/audit-log`), which records who did what and when. Assume your actions are attributable."}}

+# VibeCheck User Manual
+
+Welcome to VibeCheck — a security audit service for teams shipping AI-generated code. This manual shows you how to use the platform day to day.
+
+## Table of Contents
+1. [Signing In](#signing-in)
+2. [Starting a New Audit (Clients)](#starting-a-new-audit-clients)
+3. [The Review Queue (Analysts)](#the-review-queue-analysts)
+4. [Viewing Your Report](#viewing-your-report-clients)
+5. [Accepting Terms & Unlocking the Report](#accepting-terms--unlocking-the-report)
+6. [Marking Findings as Remediated](#marking-findings-as-remediated)
+7. [Requesting a Re‑Scan](#requesting-a-rescan)
+8. [Billing & Subscription (Simulated)](#billing--subscription-simulated)
+9. [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
+
+---
+
+## 1. Signing In
+
+Open the app at `http://localhost:3210/login`.
+
+You'll see demo accounts on the page. Click the button for your role, or fill in your own email/password:
+
+| Role | Email | Password | What you can do |
+|------|-------|----------|-----------------|
+| **Analyst** | `analyst@vibecheck.dev` | `Analyst123!` | Triage findings, sign off reports, finalize audits |
+| **Client (Acme)** | `client@acme.dev` | `Client123!` | View delivered audits, mark remediation, request re‑scans |
+| **Admin (operator)** | `admin@vibecheck.dev` | `Admin123!` | See all engagements, clients, audit log |
+
+> **Note**: These are prototype accounts. In a production deployment, you would sign up through your organization's invite system.
+
+After signing in, you're routed to the page that matches your role.
+
+---
+
+## 2. Starting a New Audit (Clients)
+
+Only clients can start new audits. From the dashboard (`/portal`), click **New audit**.
+
+### The 4-step intake form
+
+| Step | What you do |
+|------|-------------|
+| **1. Engagement name** | Give it a recognizable name, e.g., "Acme payments API — pre‑launch". |
+| **2. Audit tier** | Choose one: |
+| | • **Quick Scan** ($399) — fast, 48‑hour turnaround. Covers OWASP checks, AI‑code patterns, secrets, and dependencies. An analyst gives every finding a decision. |
+| | • **Full Audit** ($2,500) — includes everything in Quick Scan plus a deep analyst triage, prioritized remediation plan, and one verification re‑scan. Turnaround: ~5 business days. |
+| | • **Continuous Monitoring** ($499/month) — scheduled re‑scans and PR‑triggered checks going forward. You'll get a monthly invoice. |
+| **3. Source** | Pick how you give us code to review: |
+| | • **Demo repo** — use the built‑in sample (good for trying the product). |
+| | • **Upload .zip** — drag a repository zip (max 25 MB, expands to max 40 MB with up to 3,000 files). Do **not** include `node_modules`, `.git`, or secrets you haven't rotated. |
+| | • **Public repo** — paste a public GitHub/GitLab URL (`https://github.com/owner/repo`). Private repos are not supported in this prototype. |
+| **4. Intake context** (optional) | Add any notes the analyst should know: recent AI‑assisted rewrite, risky areas, launch date, compliance concerns, etc. This helps them prioritize. |
+
+After step 4, the engagement is created and the scan starts automatically. You'll be taken to the engagement page where you can watch the progress.
+
+### What happens after you submit
+
+| Status | Meaning | Your action |
+|--------|---------|-------------|
+| **Intake** | Submitted, queued | None |
+| **Scanning** | Automated pass running | Wait — the page refreshes itself. |
+| **Scan failed** | Ingestion or engine error | Check the error message; contact your analyst if you're unsure. |
+| **Analyst review** | A human is reviewing every finding | This is the service. No action needed from you. |
+| **Ready for client** | Report is finalized, waiting for you | **Accept the terms** (next section). |
+| **Delivered** | Report available | Start marking findings remediated or request a re‑scan. |
+| **Remediation** | You're fixing findings | Mark progress, then request a re‑scan when ready. |
+| **Closed** | Engagement complete | None. |
+
+---
+
+## 3. The Review Queue (Analysts)
+
+If you sign in as the analyst, you see the **review desk** at `/analyst`. This is your work list.
+
+### Queue summary
+
+At the top you see:
+- **Percent triaged** — a progress bar. Turns green when you've decided every finding.
+- **Open / total** — how many findings still need a decision.
+- **Confirmed / dismissed** — quality metrics.
+- **Review gate** — "Signed off" or "Not signed off" with the timestamp of when you signed.
+
+### Per-engagement card
+
+Each engagement card shows:
+- The tier (Quick Scan, Full Audit, Monitoring).
+- Risk score and grade (e.g., "100 / F" means high severity everywhere).
+- Severity breakdown (critical, high, medium, low, info).
+- Scan stats (files scanned, how long it took).
+- An auto‑refresh indicator (the page updates itself while a scan runs).
+
+### Triage each finding
+
+Expand a finding to see the rule, file, line, redacted code snippet, description, and remediation guidance.
+
+For each finding, choose one:
+
+| Button | What it does |
+|--------|--------------|
+| **Confirm finding** | Marks this as a real issue. You can set a priority (P0 — now, P1 — this sprint, P2 — scheduled, P3 — backlog), write an analyst comment (the client will see this), and optionally edit the title/description/remediation that the client sees. |
+| **Dismiss / false positive** | Marks this as not a real issue. Write a brief reason in the comment (e.g., "Test fixture, not production code"). This counts toward the false‑positive rate, so be deliberate. |
+| **Reopen** | If you inherit a decided finding and disagree, use this to retriage it. Resets sign‑off, so you'll need to sign off again later. |
+| **Bulk confirm** (right rail) | Confirm every OPEN finding at or above a confidence threshold (50–95%) in one click. Still requires a subsequent sign‑off. |
+| **Add analyst finding** | Use this for issues the static engine can't see — missing authorization on a specific handler, a trust‑boundary crossed without validation, a secrets‑management gap, or a business‑logic flaw. You give it a title, severity, category, file/line, description, remediation, and confidence. This finding will appear in the report and survive re‑scans. |
+
+### Signing off
+
+When every finding has a decision (0 open), the **sign‑off panel** appears in the right rail.
+
+1. **Write a sign‑off note** (optional but recommended). This records your assumptions, caveats, and anything the client must know to read the report correctly. This note becomes the "analyst note" in the final report.
+2. Press **Complete analyst review**. The engagement records the sign‑off, logs it in the audit trail, and moves to `UNDER_REVIEW` → `READY_FOR_CLIENT`.
+
+> **Important**: Any later triage change (confirm, dismiss, reopen, bulk confirm) clears the sign‑off. You'll need to sign off again after changing any decision.
+
+### Finalizing the report
+
+After sign‑off, a **finalization panel** appears with a generated executive summary.
+
+1. **Edit the executive summary** if needed. It should stand alone for a non‑technical reader: what was reviewed, the headline risk, the top 2‑3 things to fix first, and the most important caveat. Keep the generated structure if it's accurate; remove boilerplate that doesn't apply.
+2. Press **Finalize report vN**. The server builds an immutable payload from confirmed findings only, marks the report `FINAL`, and moves the engagement to `READY_FOR_CLIENT`. This is logged as `report.finalized`.
+
+The report is now immutable. Corrections require a new scan and a new report version — there is no edit path, by design.
+
+---
+
+## 4. Viewing Your Report (Clients)
+
+Once the analyst has finalized the report and the engagement is `READY_FOR_CLIENT`, the report unlocks **only after you accept the service terms**.
+
+### Accepting terms
+
+1. Open the engagement page. You'll see a short terms panel.
+2. Read the prototype terms (or open the full terms at `/terms` if you want the complete text).
+3. Check the **I accept the service terms** checkbox.
+4. Press the unlock button.
+
+Acceptance is recorded with your user, timestamp, and the engagement in the audit log. It's not a per‑report click‑through that can be dismissed — it unlocks delivery for that engagement. If a colleague needs to accept, they must sign in with their own account.
+
+### What the report contains
+
+When the report opens, you'll see:
+
+- **Engagement & scope** — what was reviewed, the tier, files scanned, engine version, scan duration. Check this first; a truncated scan limits what the report can tell you.
+- **Executive summary** — the analyst's framing of the headline risk and what to fix first. Written for a non‑technical reader.
+- **Risk score & grade** — 0–100 (higher is worse) with letter grades A–F. This is a prioritization aid, not a certification.
+- **Severity counts** — how many critical, high, medium, low, info findings.
+- **Findings** — each with:
+  - Severity and OWASP category (e.g., A02: Cryptographic Failures)
+  - Source family (AI-code rules, secrets, dependencies, license, or analyst)
+  - File path and line number
+  - **Redacted** code snippet (raw credentials are never shown)
+  - Analyst's explanation of why this matters
+  - Remediation guidance (how to fix it)
+  - Priority (P0–P3) — your remediation order
+- **Analyst note** — scope assumptions and caveats from the sign‑off.
+- **Methodology & limitations** — what was and was not tested.
+- **Disclaimer** — the report is not a certification or compliance attestation.
+
+### Print-friendly view
+
+Use the **print button** on the report page for a print‑friendly view or to save as PDF via your browser.
+
+### Report version history
+
+The engagement page shows how many report versions exist. Each finalization creates a new version (v1, v2, …). Earlier versions are immutable history; you can't edit them, but you can compare them if you request a re‑scan.
+
+---
+
+## 5. Accepting Terms & Unlocking the Report
+
+This is a one‑time step per engagement.
+
+1. On the engagement page, look for the **terms panel** near the top.
+2. Read the short terms (or click **View full terms** to open `/terms`).
+3. Check the **I accept** box.
+4. The **Unlock report** button becomes active. Click it.
+
+The engagement status changes to `DELIVERED`, and the remediation tracker and re‑scan button appear.
+
+> **Why is this here?** The service terms are a prototype placeholder, not legal advice. In production they would be counsel‑reviewed contracts that a client must accept before receiving a security audit report.
+
+---
+
+## 6. Marking Findings as Remediated
+
+After the report is delivered, the engagement enters the `REMEDIATION` phase. You mark findings that you've fixed.
+
+### How to mark a finding remediated
+
+1. On the engagement page, go to the **Remediation** section (appears after delivery).
+2. Find the confirmed finding you fixed.
+3. Click **Mark as remediated**.
+4. Optionally add a note describing the fix (commit SHA, PR number, change summary).
+5. The finding's `clientStatus` flips from `OPEN` to `REMEDIATED`, and `remediatedAt` is set.
+
+### Progress counters
+
+- **Open** — confirmed findings you haven't marked remediated yet.
+- **Remediated** — findings you've marked fixed.
+- When the first finding is marked remediated and the engagement was `DELIVERED`, the status switches to `REMEDIATION`.
+
+> **Remember**: Marking a finding remediated is your assertion that it's fixed. The **re‑scan** is the verification step. Only findings in the current final report can be tracked; stale findings from older scan versions are read‑only history.
+
+### Requesting a re‑scan when you're done
+
+1. In the Remediation section, click **Request re‑scan**.
+2. Requirements (the button is disabled until they're met):
+   - You have accepted the terms.
+   - There is a final report.
+   - The source snapshot is still retained (retention defaults to 30 days; continuous‑monitoring engagements keep it longer).
+   - No scan is currently queued or running.
+3. The re‑scan runs the engine against the **retained snapshot** — not your local working copy. If you fixed code after uploading, the platform won't see those fixes. For a materially changed codebase, start a new engagement and upload the current code, or ask the operator.
+4. When the scan completes, you get a new draft report and a comparison strip showing resolved/new/outstanding findings and the score delta.
+5. The engagement returns to `UNDER_REVIEW`. The analyst triages new findings, signs off, and finalizes a new report version. Prior analyst decisions carry forward by fingerprint, so the review doesn't start from scratch — but new code still gets human review.
+
+If the source was purged by retention, the re‑scan cannot run — you must upload a fresh snapshot.
+
+---
+
+## 7. Billing & Subscription (Simulated)
+
+In this prototype, billing doesn't charge real money. It records simulated invoices and subscriptions in the database.
+
+### What you see on `/portal/billing`
+
+- **Current plan** — your tier (NONE, MONITORING, etc.).
+- **Invoices** — a ledger of simulated paid invoices.
+- **Subscription status** — active, past due, canceled.
+- **Audit tiers** — reference prices:
+  - Quick Scan: $399 (one‑time)
+  - Full Audit: $2,500 (one‑time)
+  - Continuous Monitoring: $499/month (recurring)
+
+### Starting an audit creates a simulated invoice
+
+When you create a new engagement, a paid invoice is written to the database with:
+- A simulated provider reference (`sim_<uuid>`).
+- Status `PAID`.
+- No card is charged.
+
+### Upgrading to Continuous Monitoring
+
+If you're on a one‑time tier and want ongoing coverage:
+1. Go to **Billing** → **Upgrade subscription**.
+2. The interface mirrors a Stripe checkout callback — it creates/extends a monthly subscription and flips your organization plan to `MONITORING`.
+3. You'll see a recurring invoice and the platform will allow scheduled re‑scans going forward (Phase 2 connector not yet built in this prototype).
+
+### No real payment details are ever entered
+
+There is no payment form, no provider connection, and no live charges. If you need real billing, replace the `runSimulatedCheckout()` module in `src/lib/billing.ts` with a Stripe integration.
+
+---
+
+## 8. Troubleshooting
+
+| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
+|---------|--------------|------------|
